messages:
sara_sales: Hi team — kicking off the FinHealth private POC. They want Redwood Private in their VPC (air-gapped option) on 4x A100 nodes (RHEL 8). Can we confirm pre-install checklist and what access we need from them?

jordan_se: Great — main things: GPU driver + CUDA compatibility, k8s version and CRI, network egress for model downloads (or offline bundle), KMS connectivity for keys. Also confirm OS kernel + secureboot state.

mike_sre: Quick pre-check commands for them to run on the nodes (ask them to paste outputs):
```
# GPU + driver
nvidia-smi -q | head -n 20
modinfo nvidia | grep -E 'version|license' || true
# kernel headers
rpm -q kernel-headers || uname -r
# dmesg for driver errors
sudo dmesg | grep -i nvrm || true
# k8s
kubectl version --short
kubectl get nodes -o wide
# container runtime
crictl version || docker --version
```

aleks_devops: Also need:
- kernel version (we recommend >= 5.10 for A100 stacks, but we can support older with caveats)
- is UEFI Secure Boot enabled? unsigned NVIDIA driver requires MOK signing or disabled secureboot
- RDMA/mellanox drivers if they plan RDMA for GPUDirect (Mellanox OFED + firmware)
- storage class for PVs and default provisioner (we need RWX for some test workloads)

tim_cust_finhealth: Thanks — I can run these tonight and paste results. We are air-gapped for regs; no outbound internet except to our KMS endpoint (internal). Also curious about how long Redwood takes to provide an offline bundle and whether you need SSH to nodes.

jordan_se: For air-gapped: we provide an offline install bundle (images + helm charts + RPMs). Typical turnaround: 1 business day to stage bundle once we have a signed NDA + target OS/kernel list. We will need SFTP/HTTP access to a host in their network to upload the bundle, or they can pull from an internal registry.

mike_sre: For validation we need temporary SSH (bastion) or kube-admin credentials with cluster-admin role. If they prefer no SSH: kubeconfig + ability to create DaemonSet and view logs is enough. We run lightweight smoke DaemonSet to verify drivers, mounts, and cgroup settings.

sara_sales: Pricing question from the customer: they want ballpark comparison Dedicated reserved pool vs Private on-prem license for 4 GPUs initial POC and then 32 GPUs if we go prod. Can someone paste the short guidance we give?

jordan_se: Short answer: POC pricing is typically a usage-based hourly for Dedicated eval vs time-limited Private eval license (one-off infra+support fee). For 4 GPUs POC we usually do a 30-day eval credit for Hosted/Dedicated or a Private trial license. For 32 GPUs in prod, we recommend a Dedicated commit for throughput predictability, or Private if data residency/compliance prevents cloud. Solutions/BD will follow up with numbers.

aleks_devops: Back to tech: kubelet settings we check: cgroup driver (systemd recommended), kube-reserved and eviction thresholds, CRI runtime config for GPU device plugin. Example device-plugin DaemonSet check:
```
kubectl -n kube-system get ds | grep device-plugin
kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset
```

mike_sre: Firewall and ports: ensure egress allowed for S3 endpoints (if using online) and HTTPS to our control-plane (if using Private with hosted control-plane). For fully air-gapped Private, control-plane sits inside their VPC and we validate: TCP 443 (control plane), SSH 22 (for support, optional), 10250 (kubelet), 2379-2380 (etcd), and any internal service ports we provide in install docs.

tim_cust_finhealth: We have internal KMS (HashiCorp Vault) behind a load balancer on 10.1.2.3. Will Redwood integrate?

jordan_se: Yes — we support Vault via transit and PKCS#11 for HSMs. Need Vault root path and service account/role with unwrap/crypto permissions. For air-gapped, provide CA cert + endpoint.

aleks_devops: Helpful logs to collect for triage if driver fails: /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, sudo dmesg | tail -n 200, journalctl -u kubelet -n 200. If module fails to load check `modprobe nvidia` output and `lsmod | grep nvidia`.

mike_sre: CUDA/driver compatibility quick guidance (send to customer):
- If they want CUDA 11.x (legacy workloads) use NVIDIA driver >= 450 (but we recommend 515+ for stability).
- CUDA 12.x => driver 520+.
(We will confirm exact mapping for model ops; provide mapping doc in bundle.)

sara_sales: Customer also sent a security questionnaire asking about data flows during POC — do we have a short blurb about what leaves the VPC during offline vs online?

jordan_se: Blurb: "During an air-gapped Private POC with offline bundle, no model weights or telemetry leave the customer's VPC. If using our hosted control plane, minimal telemetry/alerts (health checks, anonymized metrics) are sent to Redwood endpoints only with explicit customer consent. We can disable outbound telemetry for the trial."

tim_cust_finhealth: Ok will run checks and share outputs by tomorrow morning. Also need estimated validation window — how long to do smoke tests once we give kube-admin?

aleks_devops: Smoke validation usually 1 working day for our SRE/DevOps to run through checks and surface blockers. Full install + integration (KMS, logging, RBAC tuning) ~ 3-5 business days depending on access and any firmware/driver fixes.

mike_sre: If we hit driver/kernel mismatch we often need node reboot and possibly kernel-headers install + DKMS rebuild for driver. That adds 1 day typically. If Secure Boot fixes required (signing or disabling) add coordination with their security team.

sara_sales: Perfect. My ask to FinHealth: run the commands Mike pasted, confirm Secure Boot state, provide kube-admin or bastion SSH window, and confirm whether they want offline bundle or outbound allowed for S3. I’ll send a short checklist and NDA request. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-checklist-template.pdf uploaded to the thread — https://redwood.internal/artifacts/deploy-checklist-template.pdf

tim_cust_finhealth: Thanks everyone — sending outputs now and will review NDA. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

jordan_se: One more note: if they plan model quantization on CPU fallback paths, we need extra CPU headroom for batching. Ask them expected qps and latency SLOs so we can recommend node sizing.

sara_sales: Will collect QPS/SLOs and share. Thanks team! :rocket:
